**Repaired finding: Deviation** (was: compliant).

My first pass searched only for solicitation/hiring verbs, which returned nothing, so I concluded the rule was satisfied. Scanning the full outline surfaced **§ 12.4**, which I had not read:

> "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

Why this fails the rule:
- **Duration** — twenty-four months post-term, sitting at the playbook walk-away boundary rather than the 12-month fallback.
- **Scope** — unlimited (any product or service, any territory), far broader than personnel directly involved in the Services.
- **No carve-out** — nothing preserving general advertising, general recruitment, or unsolicited approaches.
- **Internal contradiction** — § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." § 12.4 grants exactly what § 12.3 disclaims.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** delete § 12.4 in full — the minimal edit reaching the preferred position of no restrictive covenant binding Customer, and it restores consistency with § 12.3. The counterparty comment offers the fallback (mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) if Copperleaf needs personnel protection.

Note for the wider review: § 12.4 also overlaps with any non-compete/exclusivity rule, and § 2.1 (take-or-pay) and § 2.2 (sole and exclusive provider) contain related Customer-side commitments that likewise conflict with § 12.3 — worth confirming those are covered by their own rules.
